subject: Comparing # of points in different landcovers for raw data vs effective sample size points

messages.author: 715d2ec20635a131
messages.subject: Comparing # of points in different landcovers for raw data vs effective sample size points
parts:
Hello dear CTMMers,

Would appreciate your advice!

I am working on a simple descriptive table showing the varying number of a birds' location fixes across different landcover types. I am hoping to compare this quantity for raw location fixes, manually filtered fixes, and supposed effective sample size "fixes" once movement models are fit. 

While the first two are straightforward to attain, I am curious if there is a direct way to quantify how many location points would fall into different landcover classes for the fitted effective sample size dataset.  Would a proportion instead of discrete # be better for this comparison?

Thanks very much in advance for your help!

Philipp

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Comparing # of points in different landcovers for raw data vs effective sample size points
parts:
Hi Phillipp,

I'm not exactly sure what you mean in the last case. The equivalent number of IID samples in that habitat? That's a good question. Both temporal autocorrelation in movement + spatial correlation in the landcover type would together cause pseudoreplication in the number of locations sampled in that landcover type. With simulations from a null model, you could get p-values. If you really needed N_effective, you could probably then backsolve from those p-values.

Best,
Chris
